key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Gradual, over hours to days, often post-viral or post-pneumonia. LOCATION: Lateral chest wall, unilateral. DURATION: Days to weeks. CHARACTER: SHARP, STABBING, PLEURITIC (worse with breathing). AGGRAVATING: DEEP INSPIRATION, cough, chest movement. RELIEVING: Splinting chest, shallow breathing, lying on affected side. TIMING: Constant but fluctuates with breathing. SEVERITY: 5-8/10 with deep breath. KEY POSITIVES: Recent respiratory infection, pleural friction rub on exam, worse with breathing/cough, unilateral. KEY NEGATIVES: NOT cardiac radiation (arm/jaw), NOT exertional, NOT crushing pressure.
